intro: Searching for a leasehold surveyor near you usually means you own a flat or maisonette on a long lease and you need to understand what your lease is worth, what extending it might involve, or whether the service charges you are being asked to pay stack up. A leasehold surveyor can value a lease extension or a freehold purchase and advise on service charges, which is quite different from the work a surveyor does when you buy a property. We can introduce you to a suitable UK surveying practice near you, and they will quote you directly, price on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a leasehold surveyor usually need
need_lead: Most people who look for a leasehold surveyor near them are trying to put a figure on something before they commit to a formal process.
needs: You have owned your flat for a while and want to know what a lease extension is likely to be worth before you approach your freeholder.
You are buying a flat with a short lease and need to understand how the remaining term affects the valuation.
You have received a service charge demand that seems high and want advice on whether the charges are reasonable.
You are thinking about buying your freehold collectively with other leaseholders and want to understand the valuation issues first.
You are a leaseholder who has already started a statutory claim and need professional input on the figures before deadlines pass.
context_heading: Understanding lease length and marriage value
context: The number of years left on a lease has a direct effect on its value, and a short lease can be worth noticeably less than a long one. Marriage value is the extra value that can arise when a lease is extended, and it has been subject to reform, so the rules that apply to your situation may not be the same as those you have read about in older guidance.

Statutory processes around lease extensions and freehold purchases have deadlines, and missing them can cost you time and money. A leasehold surveyor can talk you through the valuation side, but they cannot give you legal advice, so it is worth speaking to a solicitor as well.
tell_heading: What to tell us when you enquire
tell: Tell us the property type and where it is, so we can introduce you to a surveying practice that covers your area.
Include the approximate number of years left on the lease, as this is central to any valuation.
Mention whether you are extending your lease, buying the freehold, or querying service charges, as these need different expertise.
Say whether you have already served notice or received anything from your freeholder, so the surveyor knows what stage you are at.
Let us know if there is a deadline you are working towards, so the practice can tell you whether they can help in time.
Add anything unusual about the property, such as a shared freehold or a lease with ground rent terms that have changed.
questions: Are you a member of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, and is your firm regulated by RICS?
Which type of report will I receive, and what will it cover?
Are you independent of the sale or of my freeholder?
How will you approach the valuation of my lease extension, and what information do you need from me?
Can you explain how marriage value applies to my situation following the recent reforms?
What are the deadlines in my statutory process, and how do they affect the valuation work?

faqs.q: What does a leasehold surveyor actually do?
faqs.a: A leasehold surveyor values lease extensions and freehold purchases and advises on service charges. This is a valuation role rather than a building survey, so it is worth being clear about what you need before you enquire.

faqs.q: How do I check a surveyor's credentials?
faqs.a: Many surveyors are members of the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors, and RICS-regulated firms must follow professional standards, hold insurance and offer a complaints process. Chartered surveyors use the letters MRICS or FRICS, and you can check the RICS directory.

faqs.q: Does a short lease really affect the value?
faqs.a: Yes, lease length affects valuation, and a short lease can reduce what a flat is worth and make it harder to mortgage. A leasehold surveyor can explain how the remaining term feeds into the figures for your property.

faqs.q: Can iComply advise me on my lease?
faqs.a: No, we are an introduction service and we do not give professional advice or provide the surveying service itself. We introduce you to a suitable UK surveying practice, who will quote you directly, and you can also speak to a solicitor about the legal side.
